title: Bathroom Renovation Ideas That Add Value in Winnipeg Homes
metaTitle: Bathroom Renovation Ideas That Add Value in Winnipeg
metaDescription: Bathroom renovation ideas that add value in Winnipeg homes: waterproofing, ventilation, storage and accessibility upgrades, plus where you can save.
excerpt: The bathroom upgrades that add value are mostly the ones that keep the room dry, easy to use and easy to clean. Here is where to spend, where to save, and which ideas make sense whether you plan to stay or sell.
answer: The bathroom upgrades that add the most value protect the house and make the room easier to live with: proper waterproofing, an exhaust fan vented outdoors, good lighting, practical storage and durable, easy-to-clean finishes. Accessibility features such as wall backing for future grab bars add long-term value at low cost while the walls are open.

faqs.q: Which bathroom renovation adds the most value?
faqs.a: Usually the work that fixes or prevents problems: a properly waterproofed shower, ventilation that vents outdoors, better lighting and a practical vanity. These make the bathroom reliable and pleasant to use every day. Purely decorative upgrades add less, and moving plumbing adds cost without necessarily adding value to the finished room.

faqs.q: Should I remove the only bathtub in my house?
faqs.a: Think carefully before you do. Households with young children often want a tub somewhere in the house, and some buyers look for one. If you have two bathrooms, a common approach is to keep a tub in one and put a walk-in shower in the other, which covers both needs.

faqs.q: Are heated bathroom floors worth it in Winnipeg?
faqs.a: If the floor is being replaced anyway, electric floor heating is a modest addition that makes tile comfortable through a long winter. It needs electrical work and a thermostat, so plan it before the new floor goes down. Adding it later means taking up the tile, which costs far more than doing it now.

faqs.q: How long does a bathroom renovation take?
faqs.a: Most bathrooms we renovate take two to three weeks of on-site work, from demolition to the final caulking. Moving plumbing, enlarging the room or ordering custom glass can add time. If it is your only bathroom, mention it at the on-site visit so the schedule gets the toilet back in service as early as possible.

blocks.x: Search for bathroom remodel return on investment in Canada and you will find percentages that look precise. They come from different markets, years and methods, and none of them can tell you what your bathroom will add to your house.
A more useful question is which upgrades protect the house, make daily life easier and will still look reasonable in ten years. That is what this guide covers.
Which bathroom upgrades add the most value?

Function and durability come first: waterproofing behind the tile, ventilation, lighting, storage and fixtures that are easy to use. They protect the house and make the room work every day. Style matters too, but people notice a bathroom that is dry, bright and practical before they notice a fashionable tile.

blocks.x: Why do waterproofing and ventilation matter most?

Because water damage is the costliest bathroom problem and the hardest to see. A shower needs a waterproof membrane and a properly sloped base under the tile, and the room needs an exhaust fan vented outdoors, not into the attic. Health Canada recommends running the fan during a shower or bath and for at least 30 minutes afterwards.

Health Canada also recommends keeping indoor humidity between 30 and 50 per cent, and repairing cracked tile, grout and caulking around tubs and showers promptly. On our [bathroom renovations](/services/bathroom-renovations), the waterproofing goes on before any tile, and we show you any water damage we find under the old shower before it is repaired.

blocks.x: Is a walk-in shower better than a tub?

For a bathroom used every day by adults, a walk-in shower is often the better choice: it is easier to step into and simpler to clean. Families with young children usually still want a tub somewhere in the house. If you have two bathrooms, a tub in one and a walk-in shower in the other covers both needs.

A curbless shower needs the floor sloped to the drain, which can mean changes to the floor framing, so it costs more than a shower with a low curb. CMHC also describes a lower-cost option for people with limited mobility: cutting an opening into the side of an existing tub so it can be used as a walk-in shower.
Which accessibility ideas are worth adding now?

The ones that are cheap while the walls are open and expensive later. CMHC notes that plywood backing on bathroom walls allows grab bars and handrails to be installed later. Slip-resistant flooring, lever-style taps, a handheld shower on a long hose and a toilet at a comfortable height help people of every age.
Plywood backing around the toilet, tub and shower, so grab bars can go anywhere they are needed.
Slip-resistant floor tile, especially near the shower.
A single-lever tap that is easy to use with wet or weak hands.
Shower controls placed where they can be reached before stepping under the water.
A vanity with a counter beside the sink for setting things down.
Where can you save without losing value?

Keep the toilet, shower drain and vanity where they are, choose mid-range tile and spend the savings on what sits behind it. Moving plumbing is one of the larger cost drivers in a bathroom, while a standard-size vanity, mirror and medicine cabinet can look as good as custom. Paint, hardware and accessories are easy to change later.
Keep the existing layout unless it truly does not work.
Put the tile budget into the floor and shower walls, and paint the rest.
Choose standard sizes for the tub, vanity and shower glass.
Leave towel bars, mirrors and hardware as easy later upgrades.
Do bathroom upgrades pay off when you sell?

They can help a house sell, but how much of the cost comes back depends on your house and market. If you plan to sell soon, favour neutral finishes, fix any water damage or ventilation problems, and avoid spending well beyond what similar homes nearby offer. A local realtor can tell you what buyers expect.
If you plan to stay, choose for how you live. A bathroom that works well every day for the next fifteen years is good value even if it adds little to the sale price.
